purpose: One place that states what is done, what is open, in what order, and why. Exists because work spread across a specification, three contracts and two audit documents, and the sequence had to be re-derived from measurement at each step. Every entry below is either proven on the builder or measured against the tree; nothing here is a recollection.

baseline_for_attribution.note: the parent of the vocabulary tranche. Twelve tests fail there, unrelated to the network. A slice is green when it introduces no failure name absent from this set.

sequencing_rationale: Three measured dependencies decide the order. First O1: a detector with no invocation site is a document, so every enforcement claim in both observability contracts is currently prose, and making one detector real is worth more than adding a tenth normative rule. Second INF7 then INF8: network actuation performs no read-back and the domain has no expected-state type, so a mutation can leave a partial state nothing detects and drift cannot be computed where it is owned; both are the network breaching the coherence pattern in AGENTS.md, which requires read-back proof. Third the DAG inversion is large but inert: it is a set of tolerated edges already recorded as debt and almost fully paid, so it is repaired after the correctness defects. The workspace-wide findings P1 to P4 do not block this path. T9 through T12 stay unscheduled: they are new capability with no executor, and building them before the system can observe itself would produce more surface that cannot be verified.
critical_path_rationale: O1 first: it is the only item that makes a normative rule enforceable, and it would immediately surface organ-headscale, a mesh coordinator running at 10.10.10.40 under a name that resolves nowhere. O3 gives the domain an expected state. O2 then has something to prove a mutation against. The O9 item that preceded this was refuted by measurement and is gone. None of the four workspace-wide findings P1 to P4 blocks this path: P1 and P2 are documentation with executable detectors, P3 is bookkeeping on a set that is already paid, and P4 is an additive gate.

open_work.title: Introduce an expected-state type in cynic-network
open_work.why: grep for desired_state, expected_state and target_state in the crate returns zero. RFC-NET-001 §1.1 principle 3 and §4 both presuppose a comparison between expected and observed, and the domain that owns the telemetry cannot perform it. drift_detected is a literal set by a caller.
open_work.scope: an expected-state model so observed minus expected is computable and the domain emits drift rather than having it supplied
open_work.unblocks: O2, and the RFC's own §1.1 principle 3

open_work.title: Give network actuation a read-back proof
open_work.why: network_actuator/execution.rs contains zero occurrences of verify, read_back, observe or prove, while read_back has 1094 references elsewhere. The DNS bundle performs four independent fs::write calls, so a failure on the third leaves a partial state nothing detects.
open_work.scope: after every actuation, observe the state the action claimed to produce; a partial write is an observed state, never a silent success

open_work.title: Fix the two imperative network I/O sites and collapse the duplicated WireGuard read-back
open_work.why: watchdog.rs spawns ping directly instead of reading L2/L3 state through the host probe it already depends on; the CLI audit shells out to wg. Two crates own WireGuard read-back: cynic-host parses dump, cynic-node parses latest-handshakes.
open_work.scope: route both through cynic-network adapters and give WireGuard read-back a single owner
open_work.risk: low, two sites, no behaviour change intended

open_work.title: Pay down the tolerated ascending edges
open_work.why: layer_debt records 15 ascending edges as tolerated debt, and 14 of the 15 are genuinely imported, so the debt is real. My earlier figure of '86 files' counted call sites of edges that were already declared, which is a different measure and overstates the defect by an order of magnitude. cynic-host is the bulk at 82 files across six higher crates, then cynic-lifecycle 3 and cynic-discovery-host 1.
open_work.scope: pay the recorded edges: for each, extract the shared contract into a layer at or below L1 or move the dependent code down, then remove the edge from layer_debt.edges and from BASELINE_EDGES. P3 reconciles the three counts first.
open_work.risk: large; one target crate at a time, never a single commit

open_work.title: Resolve the DNS cutover, which is infrastructure rather than code
open_work.why: service.cynic resolves nowhere, so the six reservations the repository declares name a zone with no published record. synapse.cynic is not a published zone either: dnsmasq answers it with TTL 0 and serves no SOA and no NS, which is a hosts-file emulation. The registry the node loads is entirely legacy, with mesh CIDR 10.20.0.0/24, an RFC 1918 range RFC-NET-001 §6.2 forbids for the overlay.
sequence: publish service.cynic alongside the existing answers
project registry records into it and prove the projection by query
remove static per-host entries one at a time, each proven resolved before the next
retire synapse.cynic once nothing resolves it
reconcile the runtime registry to canonical vocabulary last
open_work.blocked_on: operator admission for resolver deployment and for mutating /etc/cynic/registry.json, which is root-owned
open_work.rollback: each step rolls back by ceasing to project; the legacy zone stays served until the last step

open_work.title: Make the taxonomy gate detect contested effective ownership
open_work.why: crate_taxonomy_ownership.rs groups crates by their manifest description, so a crate that re-exports another crate's central model under a different responsibility passes. The mesh model contested between cynic-core and cynic-network is the live instance. contracts/pruning-policy.json one_responsibility_one_crate says two crates that re-export the same surface under a second name are CONTESTED and the canonical owner wins; the gate does not implement that clause.
open_work.scope: extend the gate so a crate whose source re-exports a type it does not define, for a surface named in the policy as owned elsewhere, is reported as contested
open_work.risk: low, a test change; it may surface existing contests beyond the network

open_work.title: Stop the mesh model churn: one line, and record why the split exists
open_work.why: I claimed the mesh model was owned by the wrong crate and put it first on the critical path. That was wrong. crates/cynic-core/tests/architecture_boundary.rs:112 carries mesh_types_are_declared_in_core_not_reexported_from_an_adapter, which requires exactly what I proposed to undo, and cynic-core/src/fleet_mesh.rs:7 states the same in prose. The mesh model lives in a pure crate with no I/O and cynic-network re-exports it while keeping its own I/O in adapters/. That is the pure/impure boundary expressed in Rust, not an ownership inversion. The only real defect is that cynic-network/src/types.rs:126 says 'for backward compatibility', which is not the reason and will mislead the next reader exactly as it misled me.
open_work.scope: correct the comment to state the real reason, which is that the model is pure and cynic-network carries the I/O. Do not move the types.

open_work.title: Resolve contested responsibility and ratchet debt, not line count
open_work.why: The measurable faults are responsibility ones. Two crates own WireGuard read-back: cynic-host/wireguard_readback.rs parses dump, cynic-node/watchdog/peer_handshake.rs parses latest-handshakes. Three crates declare a DNS zone constant. cynic-discovery-host re-exports discovery from the cynic-host monolith instead of owning it. Size is where to look, not what is wrong: cynic-node's network LOC are 8898 projection, 3634 orchestration and 3929 I/O, and only two imperative I/O sites actually violate the shell boundary. Measured across the workspace: 152 declared dependencies, 124 imported, 28 never imported.
open_work.scope: resolve each contested responsibility to a single owner, repointing the loser. Size is then a consequence. Do not split a crate to satisfy a line count.

verification_discipline: never treat a size band as a verdict. contracts/pruning-policy.json split_criteria governs: a crate is justified by an independent schedule, compilation or service requirement, a reused public API, an independent test reason, or a dependency cycle. Its known_ambiguities states the too-small threshold is contextual and gives a signal, not an automatic verdict. The 5-15k band in CANONICAL_CRATE_MAP.md is a practical band, not a rule, and that file declares it is not the taxonomy authority. The 25k ceiling in foundation.json IS a hard boundary. Size locates debt; responsibility rules decide the verdict.
prove on the builder, never on cortex; cortex ICEs on rustc 1.96 and its RAM is unstable
compare against the baseline failure set every time; a slice is green when it adds no new failure name
never rsync into the canonical checkout: commit, push, then merge --ff-only on the builder

restore Cargo.lock after every builder run; cargo rewrites it without --locked, and --locked is currently unusable because the committed lockfile does not match the package dependency sets, which is pre-existing debt proven at edbf8fae
format only explicit files; never bare cargo fmt in a shared worktree
when a claim is a count, re-verify it with the command the document carries before committing; three counts in these documents were wrong when taken by hand
